chalisa.do1: Placing on my head the dust of Śrī Rādhā's lotus feet, on the bank of the Yamunā
I tell this Chālīsā, full of sweetness and the root of every blessing.
chalisa.cau1: Victory, victory to you, Bihārī, the perfect Brahman, crusher of the wicked, who take incarnation in play.
chalisa.cau2: Whoever sings of your divine play gains, without labour, all the goals of life.
chalisa.cau3: You appeared as the son of Śrī Vasudeva and Mother Devakī, together with your brother Balarāma, the bearer of the plough.
chalisa.cau4: The Lord came from Mathurā to Gokula; in Nanda's house the music of rejoicing played.
chalisa.cau5: Pūtanā came to give you poison; you gave her liberation and sent her to your abode.
chalisa.cau6: You destroyed the demon Tṛṇāvarta, and with a thrust of your foot slew Śakaṭāsura.
chalisa.cau7: In play you ate earth, and showed the whole world in your mouth.
chalisa.cau8: You ate butter in the gopīs' houses, one after another; Yaśodā had the joy of your childhood play.
chalisa.cau9: You let yourself be bound to the mortar, and freed the twin arjuna trees from their inert birth.
chalisa.cau10: You tore apart the beak of the demon Baka, and slew the fearsome Aghāsura.
chalisa.cau11: Brahmā stole the boys and the calves; he had come to beguile Mohana, the enchanter.
chalisa.cau12: Murāri became all the boys and calves; then Brahmā prayed earnestly.
chalisa.cau13: The Lord bridled the serpent Kāliya and drank up the forest fire.
chalisa.cau14: Playing with your friends you were happy, and carried Śrīdāmā on your shoulders.
chalisa.cau15: Taking away the gopīs' garments, you taught a lesson; and you lifted the great mountain on your fingernail.
chalisa.cau16: You gave the sight of yourself to the wives of the sacrificing Brahmins, and enjoyed the nectar of Rādhā's love.
chalisa.cau17: You brought Nanda back from the realm of Varuṇa, and showed the cowherds your own realm.
chalisa.cau18: Seeing the autumn moon, you played the flute, and holding the rāsa dance you gave great joy.
chalisa.cau19: You freed your father Nanda's feet from the python, and struck off Śaṅkhacūḍa's head.
chalisa.cau20: You slew Ariṣṭāsura and Keśī, and killed Vyomāsura, who came in disguise to deceive.
chalisa.cau21: Leaving distraught Braja, you came to Mathurā; you slew Kaṃsa and settled the Yadu clan.
chalisa.cau22: You freed your mother and father from prison, and gained learning in the house of Sāndīpani.
chalisa.cau23: Then you sent the wise Uddhava to Braja; seeing the love there, he forgot himself entirely.
chalisa.cau24: You made Kubjā a beautiful woman, and carried off the delicate Rukmiṇī.
chalisa.cau25: You slew Bhaumāsura and freed your devotees; conquering the gods, you brought the wish-granting tree of heaven down to earth.
chalisa.cau26: You destroyed Dantavakra and Śiśupāla, and delivered birds and beasts, King Nṛga and the hunter.
chalisa.cau27: You made the poor Sudāmā a lord of wealth, and won fame as the charioteer of Pārtha's chariot.
chalisa.cau28: You are the one who taught the knowledge of the Gītā, who dispelled Arjuna's delusion.
chalisa.cau29: You ate bananas at the house of your devotee Vidura, and brought about the war of the Mahābhārata.
chalisa.cau30: You lengthened the garment of Drupada's daughter, and saved Parīkṣit as he burned in the womb.
chalisa.cau31: You are the Tortoise, the Fish, the Boar, the lord of serpents, Vāmana, Kalki, the Buddha and the lord of sages.
chalisa.cau32: Becoming Nṛsiṃha you saved Prahlāda; taking the form of Śrī Rāma you slew Rāvaṇa.
chalisa.cau33: Victory to you, slayer of the demons Madhu and Kaiṭabha, beloved of Ambarīṣa, bearer of the discus.
chalisa.cau34: You delivered the hunter and Ajāmila, and women such as Śabarī and the courtesan.
chalisa.cau35: You who ride on Garuḍa, who cut the elephant's snare, grant the sight of you, delight of Dhruva's eyes.
chalisa.cau36: Grant the company of pure saints, so that the joy and colour of love and devotion may grow.
chalisa.cau37: Grant a dwelling in divine Vṛndāvana; may the mirage of craving and hope in the world fall away.
chalisa.cau38: Śiva, Nārada, Śuka, and Sanaka and his brothers, adepts in Brahman, meditate on you.
chalisa.cau39: Victory, victory to you, merciful beloved of Rādhā, remover of every distress and of the net of delusion.
chalisa.cau40: Obstacles, disease and heavy sorrow perish for those who remember Giridhārī, lord of the world.
chalisa.cau41: Whoever reads the Chālīsā a hundred times is given every fruit he desires, upon his head.
chalisa.cha1: Whoever reads the Gopāla Chālīsā daily, as a rule, with his mind intent on it,
takes on a divine body at the end and goes to the abode of Goloka.
All the happiness and wealth of the world that devotees seek from him,
Jayarāmadeva says, they always gain by the mercy of the guru.
chalisa.do2: Protector of those who bow to you, refuge of the shelterless, ocean of compassion, Lord of Braja:
with this Chālīsā, take me as your own, lord of my life.
